Direction depends on design: diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes raised peak flows, larger sand dams increase flooding risk, a conservation-tillage sheet from the Philippines rated flood impacts worse, and a farm pond in India was rated neutral.

effect_mechanism: Water harvesting and conservation structures capture runoff and raise soil moisture so rainfed crops yield more, especially in dry years and low-rainfall areas; stored water allows supplemental irrigation and extra crops, stone lines trap sediment and organic matter, and converting slopeland to levelled terraces increases moisture retention. In Burkina Faso stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% and by about 142% with compost, and WOCAT compilers across many technology sheets judge crop, fodder and animal production increased, citing moisture retention, regenerated grasses and better water access. Conservation agriculture meta-analyses find no-till with residue retention and rotation raises rainfed yields by 7.3% in dry climates and maize under conservation agriculture yields more where mean annual precipitation is below 600 mm [ev_crop_yield_pittel15_2, ev_crop_yield_pittel15_5, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_2]; on-farm trials in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare on planting basins and direct-seeded plots, and sand dams cut crop failure against a control catchment in Kenya and improved livestock health in Zimbabwe [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1, ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1].
conditionality: The pool mixes independent evaluations (matching studies in Ethiopia, a difference-in-difference evaluation in Rwanda) with lender self-reported completion-report figures, bundled watershed programmes that combined works with seed and crop-husbandry packages, and a large body of practitioner judgements from technology sheets. Nulls and negatives are present: conservation promoted mostly off-farm had no yield effect, late adopters and the pooled sample in Ethiopia showed no significant gain and benefits appeared only once structures were maintained for at least seven years, bunds lowered yields in high-rainfall Amhara, zai lowered sorghum yields under waterlogging in Cameroon, diversion banquettes in Niger cut yields, and keeping grazing animals off newly treated rangeland lowered animal production ratings in Niger; much of the zai gain rides on added manure or compost. Conservation agriculture meta-analyses add caveats: no-till lowers yields by 5.7% overall and also in dry climates when applied alone, yields fall under no-till in humid climates, under conservation agriculture where mean annual precipitation exceeds 1,000 mm and under mulch where waterlogging occurs, yield stability is no better than under conventional tillage and is lower in humid climates or without rotation and residues (a stability meta-analysis drawn mostly from high-income trials), and in drought seasons in Mozambique and Zimbabwe conservation agriculture gave no harvest or yielded less than conventional tillage [ev_crop_yield_pittel15_1, ev_crop_yield_pittel15_3, ev_crop_yield_pittel15_4, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_2, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3, ev_crop_yield_knapp18_1, ev_crop_yield_knapp18_3, ev_crop_yield_knapp18_4, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_8, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7].

effect_mechanism: Higher and more stable yields, irrigation of gardens and higher-value crops from stored water, and better fodder and livestock raise household income and food security; beneficiaries shift from staples to vegetables, and a quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_economic_return_mala24_1]. WOCAT compilers describe the same pathway: planting pits in Uganda keep banana stands fruiting through drought and raise harvests for sale, ripper tillage in Zambia gives better tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost, farm ponds in Cambodia supply irrigation during drought, and contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area for diverse crops [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1139_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. WOCAT compilers' own benefit-versus-cost ratings point the same way, judging the long-term returns on both establishment and maintenance positive or very positive on nearly every sheet. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1].
conditionality: Most pooled units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT technology sheets, including compilers' benefit-versus-cost judgements rather than measured returns, and much of the literature comes from bundled watershed programmes and lender completion or appraisal reports, so measured household effects are a minority. Independent evaluations are more cautious: no significant effect on food security or total income in Ethiopian programmes, terraces reducing net crop income, a Brazilian production-cistern programme with a benefit-cost ratio far below break-even, single SWC measures not covering their annual costs, and sand dams likely not cost-efficient [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1, ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_economic_return_zoug14_3, ev_economic_return_ritc21_1]. Compilers also rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and record no change on several sheets, including a subsistence farm pond in India; Kenyan sand dams sit inside a wider food-security programme, and food security, income and returns are all proxies for poverty [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Nicaragua, Jordan, Uzbekistan and Somalia, reflecting up-front costs that are only recovered over time. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1].

effect_mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income and lean-season food security [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]. WOCAT compilers add that farm ponds in Cambodia keep enough irrigation water through drought, gully check dams in Ethiopia free rangeland for grazing, and gully rehabilitation in Somalia raised crop and livestock productivity [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Compilers' benefit-versus-cost ratings are positive or very positive over the long term for every sheet that rates them. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1].
conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts, and practitioner ratings make up a large share of the pool [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. Compilers rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and an Indian subsistence farm pond as leaving farm income unchanged; Kenyan sand dams are embedded in a wider food-security programme [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Nicaragua and Somalia, and the cost-benefit units are compiler judgements, not measured returns. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1].

WOCAT compilers report continuous income from tea on bench terraces in Thailand, a per-hectare income gain from progressive bench terraces in China, contour stone bunds in Bhutan meeting household maize demand, and Gradoni terraces in Uzbekistan improving drought resilience [ev_household_income_wocat_4281_2018_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1522_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_6891_2023_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_7553_2025_risk_of_production_failure]. Compilers' benefit-versus-cost ratings are mostly positive or very positive over the long term.

A review reports terraces reducing net crop income in Ethiopia and banquette profitability in Niger was close to nil; compilers record no change in food security for vetiver terraces in Haiti, where farmers must wait for degraded soil to recover, and on sheets from Rwanda [ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_heusch95_1, ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Food security, income and returns are proxies for poverty. effect_mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and lines, banquettes, trenches, pits and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers across many countries rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced, explaining that micro-catchments cut the kinetic energy of rain by trapping runoff and that check dams slow runoff so soil accumulates upstream [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_soil_loss].
conditionality: Over two thirds of the pool are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and several literature sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Indian sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies. Negative findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. Some sheets rate no change, including the Indian farm-pond sheet, and the Zambian tillage sheet expects less downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation]. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3].

conditionality: The literature units all come from a single review of trenches, largely in the Peruvian Andes (upper-middle income), which also reports increased catchment sediment in the first years after construction; plot-level effects may not transfer to catchments [ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_3]. effect_mechanism: Pits, bunds, terraces, trenches and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1].
conditionality: Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix recharge, spring discharge and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger, and Ethiopian compilers note that off-site effects of recently built structures are yet to be assessed [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. Groundwater gains are often local and short-lived, can be wiped out by increased pumping, and year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season, and trenches had little effect on baseflow or infiltration [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2].

effect_mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil keep livestock watered while clay tanks are dry, an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns with a large drop in rural establishments without any water source, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. Stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale raise groundwater levels, and in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to runoff control and better infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1].

effect_mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams, ponds and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up. WOCAT compilers for gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dam ponds and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia, sand dams in Kenya, stone check walls in India, on-farm ponds in Cambodia and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia judge them to improve water harvesting, quantity or availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1400_2011_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1547_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_harvesting_collection_of_water]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1].
conditionality: The groundwater effect of sand dams is limited in space and time, many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. Several literature units are review citations or vote counts, the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that off-site impacts of the recently built check dam still need assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6716_2023_water_availability]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2].
